I had 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea.

Earlier I had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning: We need to log the foods. The user says they had 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea. Also earlier they had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee. We should log each item. For each log, we need to call the function log_food. We can log each item separately. For the mango: food_name: "frozen mango", portion_amount: 8, portion_unit: "piece". meal_type? Not specified; default is snack. log_date? Not specified; default null. For chai tea: food_name: "chai tea", portion_amount: 1, portion_unit: "cup" maybe? But portion_unit must be one of "cup" | "grams" | "slice" | "piece" | "tablespoon". So "cup" is valid. Portion_amount: 1. meal_type: default snack. For pepperoni pizza: food_name: "pepperoni pizza", portion_amount: 2, portion_unit: "slice". For coffee: food_name: "coffee", portion_amount: 1, portion_unit: "cup". We need to call the function for each. The user didn't specify meal times; we can use default. We'll produce separate function calls.
